title: Regional Locksmith: EU-only routing guardrail and customer permit/ban enforcement
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: Several customers require strict EU-only processing for specific workloads. Current smart router can prefer EU regions, but there is no deterministic enforcement layer that both: (1) prevents accidental cross-border processing for 'EU-only' flagged requests, and (2) lets account-level permit/ban rules override or relax the default behavior for emergency operational needs. Goal: add a lightweight guardrail service (Regional Locksmith) that enforces EU-only routing at the request level, supports customer-scoped permit/ban lists, integrates with the policy decision service, and emits audit events and metrics for compliance review. Scope: routing decisions (region + tier selection), model-variant fallback rules, permit/ban precedence and emergency bypass handshake, observability hooks for audit, and an operator rollback path. Out of scope: UI for self-service permit requests (handled in a follow-up PM ticket). Technical constraints: must work with hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; decision latency budget < 5ms added to request path; must preserve existing per-tenant routing overrides where explicitly allowed. Success metrics: 99.99% enforcement accuracy on EU-only test corpus, <5ms median added latency, and audit logs stored for 365 days for flagged accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Requests with header X-Data-Region: eu_only are only routed to EU regions or to on-prem EU deployments when account has onprem=true
Account-level ban entries (customer_bans) immediately block cross-border routing and return 403 with structured error code 'EU_CROSS_BORDER_BLOCK'
Permit entries (customer_permits) allow specified account IDs to route to non-EU tiers only when a documented emergency override token is present
Fallback model variants marked 'eu-compatible' are chosen automatically if primary model is unavailable, with transparent audit trail indicating fallback reason
Policy decisions per-request are emitted to the audit stream with correlation_id and stored for 365 days
E2E tests simulate 10k mixed-location requests and show 99.99% compliance and <5ms median decision latency
Operator can activate a time-bound global bypass for 15 minutes that is recorded in the audit log and requires two-person approval via the console API
